I read the whole file. I looked for nontrivial reasoning repeated within it or shared with nearby files in the SixPoint directory. Within the file, `firstActiveFailureSlack_nonneg` and `secondActiveFailureSlack_pos` are thin wrappers around existing lemmas. `thirdActiveFailureSlack_pos` is a single bespoke `nlinarith` argument. `activeFailureCombination_nonneg` and `activeFailureCombination_pos` are two-line `mul_nonneg`/`mul_pos` plus `linarith` proofs. The two share a pattern, but it is too short to count as repeated machinery.

The only recurring pattern is in `weightedPairScore_configuration_eq_activeFailureCombination`. It proves `hr₁`, `hr₂`, `hb₁` and `hb₂` as norm-equals-dist facts by one-line `simp` calls. The same `simp [..., SixPointConfiguration.redDisplacement, dist_eq_norm, norm_sub_rev]` lines appear in `RootEdgeFailureTree.lean` (around lines 188–191), `RootEdge.lean` (around 1194–1199), `RootEdgeType12.lean` (around 546–551) and `SiblingIncidenceLedger.lean` (line 80). That is routine unfolding, not nontrivial mathematical reasoning. The rubric says such cases are insufficient, so I did not report it. The only possible consolidation is a pair of named lemmas such as `norm_redDisplacement_eq_dist` and `norm_bluePullback_eq_dist`. That would be a minor cleanup, not a justified finding under this rubric. I did not find any other repeated nontrivial block.
